title: Food and how it is made
description: Follow a dish from the market stall to the table.
grammar: the verbs of cooking, and the words from the market to the plate
grammarNote: Most cooking verbs are regular: asar, hornear, pelar. They take the food as a direct object.

explanation.summary: A dish has a history: what it is made of, who made it and how it was cooked. This unit follows a meal from the stall where you buy it to the plate, and gives you the verbs and the nouns of that process.

sections.heading: What it is made of
sections.body: La masa is the dough of bread or pastry, and la cazuela is the pot it cooks in. At the market, cada puesto sells a few things. El aliño is what you pour over a dish, and una pizca is the smallest amount of anything: una pizca de sal.

examples.es: Compré la masa en el puesto de la esquina.
examples.en: I bought the dough at the stall on the corner.

examples.es: Echa una pizca de sal a la cazuela.
examples.en: Throw a pinch of salt into the pot.

examples.es: El aliño lleva aceite y limón.
examples.en: The dressing is made with oil and lemon.

sections.heading: The verbs of cooking
sections.body: Asar is to roast, hornear is to bake, and pelar is to peel. These verbs take a direct object: asa el pollo, hornea el pan, pela las patatas. All three keep the -ar ending in every form.

examples.es: Asa el pollo hasta que esté dorado.
examples.en: Roast the chicken until it is golden.

examples.es: Pela las patatas antes de cocerlas.
examples.en: Peel the potatoes before boiling them.

sections.heading: The taste at the end
sections.body: La marinada is the liquid a piece of food sits in before it is cooked, and la textura is how the food feels in the mouth. A dish can be ligero or pesado, and those two words tell you how much you will enjoy it.

examples.es: Dejé el pollo en la marinada toda la noche.
examples.en: I left the chicken in the marinade all night.

examples.es: La textura del arroz es muy suave.
examples.en: The texture of the rice is very soft.

examples.es: Este plato es más pesado de lo que parece.
examples.en: This dish is heavier than it seems.

items.note: Masculine: el puesto. It is a stall at a market.
Feminine: la cazuela. The deep pot a stew cooks in.
Masculine: el aliño. What you pour over a salad.
Feminine: la pizca. The smallest amount of anything.
The verb asar: aso, asas, asa.
The verb hornear: horneo, horneas, hornea.
The verb pelar: pelo, pelas, pela.

drills.meaning: throw a pinch of salt into the soup

drills.meaning: the salad has an oil dressing on it

drills.meaning: we are going to bake the bread in the oven

drills.meaning: we left the chicken in the marinade all night
